headline: $6.3 billion cyberattack hits Binance, world's largest crypto exchange
summary: The breach, potentially the largest theft in crypto history, occurred after a hacker accessed an engineer's laptop to enter internal systems.
details: The world's leading cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has suffered an unprecedented cyberattack resulting in the loss or theft of approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets.
Initial investigations reveal the breach began when a hacker compromised an engineer's laptop, gaining unauthorized access to Binance's internal systems to move vast amounts of funds.
The attack triggered a market crash; Bitcoin fell over 3% to $76,368, its lowest in six weeks, while Ether dropped over 3% to $2,178, a two-month low.
Binance's own token, BNB, plunged 5% to $709, and US stocks for Coinbase Global and MicroStrategy fell by 4.8% and 6% respectively.
In response, Binance co-founder Yi He stated that the company will personally bear all financial losses incurred by the users due to the hacking.
Collaborative efforts with other firms have already frozen approximately $3 billion in assets, including $1.57 billion by Tether, $800 million by Circle, and $200 million by Ripple.
Binance has temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals to prevent further risk, though it maintains that user core funds remain safe.
Experts warn that cybercriminals are now using artificial intelligence (AI) to launch more sophisticated attacks, posing a significant future threat to the industry.
caption:
$6.3 billion stolen. The world's largest crypto exchange just suffered one of the biggest hacks in history.

The world's leading cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has suffered an unprecedented cyberattack resulting in the loss or theft of approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets.

Initial investigations reveal the breach began when a hacker compromised an engineer's laptop, gaining unauthorized access to Binance's internal systems to move vast amounts of funds.

The attack triggered a market crash; Bitcoin fell over 3% to $76,368, its lowest in six weeks, while Ether dropped over 3% to $2,178, a two-month low.

Binance's own token, BNB, plunged 5% to $709, and US stocks for Coinbase Global and MicroStrategy fell by 4.8% and 6% respectively.

In response, Binance co-founder Yi He stated that the company will personally bear all financial losses incurred by the users due to the hacking.

Collaborative efforts with other firms have already frozen approximately $3 billion in assets, including $1.57 billion by Tether, $800 million by Circle, and $200 million by Ripple.

Binance has temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals to prevent further risk, though it maintains that user core funds remain safe.

Experts warn that cybercriminals are now using artificial intelligence (AI) to launch more sophisticated attacks, posing a significant future threat to the industry.

headline_marked: [[1,500 vehicles]] to join 11-party alliance's 410km long march to Kushtia
headline: 1,500 vehicles to join 11-party alliance's 410km long march to Kushtia
summary: An 11-party alliance is launching a 410km march from Dhaka to Kushtia, expecting around 1,500 vehicles and participants from 19 districts. The procession aims to press for seven key demands.
details: The 11-party alliance is preparing for a significant 410-kilometer long march from Dhaka to Kushtia, scheduled to commence tomorrow. Approximately 1,500 vehicles and participants from 19 different districts are anticipated to join this event.

Party Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar announced that the procession would start with over 600 vehicles, with more joining along the route. The march will traverse through Khulna, Jashore, and Jhenaidah, marking it as the longest of the alliance's three long marches to date.

The alliance is organizing this march to advocate for seven specific demands. These include the implementation of referendum verdicts, justice for the July uprising killings, resolution of shortages in electricity, oil, and gas, control over rising prices, an end to corruption and land grabbing, improved law and order, and the elimination of partisan influence in state institutions.

While acknowledging the potential disruption to public movement and businesses, Porwar stated that organizers would endeavor to use only one side of the highways to minimize inconvenience. The alliance has reportedly coordinated with police and administrative authorities in the Dhaka and Khulna ranges, securing assurances of cooperation.

Participants have been urged to maintain patience, restraint, and discipline, with provocative remarks or behavior being strictly prohibited. The event will kick off with an inaugural rally at the National Mosque Baitul Mukarram at 7:00 AM, followed by the procession's departure at 8:00 AM.

The march includes scheduled roadside rallies in various locations such as Naodoba (Shariatpur), Fakirhat (Bagerhat), Khulna city, Jashore, and Jhenaidah. The procession is expected to conclude with a final rally at Shaheed Abrar Fahad Stadium in Kushtia at 8:30 PM.
